references.text: God heard the Israelites' cry of distress and remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the same theme of God's response to the people's suffering and His faithfulness to the covenant.
God says that He has seen the Israelites' suffering and heard their cry because of their slave drivers—a parallel description of God's attention to the people's distress.
The covenant God made with Abraham, which God now remembers and acts upon.
God's eternal covenant with Abraham and his descendants, including the promise of the land of Canaan.
The covenant confirmed to Isaac—part of the covenant God remembers in Exodus 6:5.
The covenant confirmed to Jacob—part of the covenant God remembers.
God promises to remember the covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, and the covenant with the ancestors whom He brought out of Egypt.
God delivered Israel because He loved them and kept the oath He had sworn to their fathers.
Nehemiah refers to how God saw the distress of the ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea.
God remembers His covenant forever, the word He gave to a thousand generations, the covenant with Abraham and the oath to Isaac.
God saw their distress when He heard their cry of distress, and He remembered His covenant with them.
Zechariah's song of praise mentions that God shows mercy to the fathers and remembers His holy covenant, the oath He swore to Abraham.
Both verses describe the same divine revelation where God confirms that He has seen, heard, and remembered the distress of His people before the exodus.
Leviticus confirms the theological mechanism in Exodus: God's ability to 'remember' the covenant with the patriarchs is the basis for His grace.
The verses illuminate each other by linking God's remembrance of the covenant directly to the story of the exodus from Egypt.
Both verses describe the same divine revelation where God confirms that He has seen, heard, and remembered the distress of His people before the exodus.
The verses illuminate each other by showing the connection between God's remembrance of the covenant (6:5) and the purpose of the exodus (7:5).
